worldcup.title: Terry Butcher: ‘I’ve learned to live with the Hand of God goal better’
worldcup.summary: The former England centre-back answers your questions on Diego Maradona, Bobby Robson and on staying in strange places “Have you made up all these on your own?” asks Terry Butcher, sitting in a London office in the week he is presented with his England legacy cap. It turns out dozens of Guardian readers want to pick the brains of a much-loved centre-back who was feted en route to a World Cup semi-final and tormented four years previously by the mercurial genius of Diego Maradona. Did Maradona ever admit to the “Hand of God”? Butcher found himself in the post-match doping-control room alongside his nemesis at the Azteca in 1986. “I tapped my head, then my hand, and then he tapped his head,” Butcher says. “He didn’t admit to it because, if he had, I’d have been right across that room.” Continue reading...

magazine.title: A long wait, some magic and that smile: Ronaldinho savours Ravenna debut at 46
magazine.summary: Brazilian legend, an investor at Serie C club, showed glimpses of old brilliance as he played 45 minutes for the promotion-chasing side It may have been the longest buildup in world football. In June the former Barcelona and Brazil legend Ronaldinho was unveiled by Italian Serie C side Ravenna, to make his comeback at the age of 46 – 11 years after his last official game. Then silence. But on a chilly November day on the eastern coast of Italy, there he was, not only in the squad but in the starting XI for the eagerly anticipated derby against Forlì as Ravenna chase promotion to Serie B. general.title: European football body’s plan to go global leaves Fifa on tenterhooks
general.summary: Findings of ‘feasibility study’ into quest for world domination loom with Europe’s wealthiest certain to benefit whatever the outcome It will be one of the most eagerly anticipated documents in football circles, assuming its contents are ever fully revealed. In September the increasingly powerful European Football Clubs body announced a “feasibility study” into exactly how it can become established on a more global scale, morphing into an organisation that represents clubs all over the world. The study’s findings could, some leading figures in the sport’s governance believe, define football’s long-term future. It has the potential to transform a landscape destabilised by the scandals surrounding Fifa and Gianni Infantino. Once considered a lobby group representing clubs’ interests in the face of domineering governing bodies, EFC has mushroomed into a behemoth with almost 1,000 members that has the potential to supplant them. Continue reading...
